messages:
SRE Oncall: alert - full heartbeat loss from eu-west4 control plane and inference fleet, dashboards show node_heartbeat=0 and all GPU nodes NotReady. automatic region health detector flagged a full outage. initiating incident.
ops-bot: automated policy: routed traffic away from eu-west4 to eu-west1 + eu-central1, canary weight 20% -> 80% shift in progress. :rotating_light:
Alex W: copy. I'm starting graceful drain for stateful workloads and blocking new scheduling into eu-west4. running:
```bash
kubectl cordon -l region=eu-west4
kubectl drain -l region=eu-west4 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```
Alex W: will pause batch provisioning jobs and mark Dedicated pools in eu-west4 read-only.
Maya R: notifying sales/support for customers with reserved capacity in eu-west4. prepping status note for portal. @SRE Oncall, do we want routing to prefer eu-central1 for low-latency customers?
SRE Oncall: yes, prefer eu-central1 for EU low-latency. eu-west1 for cost-sensitive. update routing priorities and enforce capacity caps to avoid oversubscribe.
Jin H: checking autoscaler logs — we see failed attachment calls to provider API and BGP withdraws. suspect upstream network event. running provider check now.
Network Eng: provider ticket opened (ref: PROVIDER-8943). they report an optical splice incident affecting multiple POPs in the region. ETA unknown. working on alternate transit but likely hours.
Alex W: plan: 1) Stop new scheduling to eu-west4 2) Drain active inference pods to preserved caches 3) Rehome long-running Dedicated pools to eu-central1/eu-west1 4) Increase burst capacity in other regions and temporarily raise quota limits. executing.
Maya R: I'll draft customer-facing note and include mitigation steps, estimated impact, and contacts. moving to status channel after bridge created.
SRE Oncall: opened bridge -> zoom.link/bridge-placeholder. Ops roles: Alex W lead evac, Jin H network liaison, Maya R comms, Network Eng on provider. escalate to Eng Infra if provider ETA > 2h.
Jin H: command snippets for rehome (run from control plane):
```bash
redwoodctl region drain --region eu-west4 --mode graceful --target-regions eu-central1,eu-west1
redwoodctl reroute --policy latency-preferred --exclude eu-west4
```
ops-bot: policy update applied: latency-preferred routing now excludes eu-west4, cache warm-up enabled in eu-central1.
Alex W: draining GPUs - checkpointing KV caches before eviction. this will slightly increase token latency during warmup.
Maya R: flagged top 5 customers on SLA watchlist and DM'd account owners. also created status incident note draft.
SRE Oncall: next steps: monitor failover success, confirm no data plane splits, hold autoscaler at safe headroom, keep ops channel updated every 10m. If provider ETA slips past 2h, prepare controlled uplift of on-demand capacity in APAC to cover critical EU bursts overnight.
Network Eng: provider now reports partial transit restored on one POP, but control plane heartbeats still intermittent. will update ticket with traceroutes.
Alex W: partial traffic back to eu-west4 blocked until control plane fully healthy. continuing drains and rehomes. :white_check_mark:
Maya R: posting brief status to status.redwood (draft ready) and pinging legal for possible regulatory notif if outage extends >4h.
SRE Oncall: thanks team. keep updates short and exact. next check-in +10m.
_meta: generated for dataset - single Slack thread representing initial triage and coordination for a full region outage
